paper.title: Online Individualized Treatment Selection under Partial Feedback: False Discovery Control and Minimax Optimality

settings.name_in_paper: Online individualized treatment selection under partial feedback (FDR-constrained)
unmapped: Asymptotic false discovery rate constraint (FDR_T <= alpha) on treated units; the learner knows the target level alpha
Regret is gap-weighted disagreement with an FDR-constrained oracle threshold rule on the local null risk l(x)=F_1(b_0(x)|x)
Historical randomized-trial sample available before online phase
Unknown covariate-specific control reference b_0(x) must be estimated; null indicators are not directly observed
settings.definition_quote: Following assignment, we observe only the potential outcome under the assigned treatment, $Y_t=A_tY_t(1)+(1-A_t)Y_t(0)=Y_t(A_t)$, while the counterfactual outcome remains unobserved. ... \Regret_T=\Ebb[\sum_{t=1}^T|\ell(\bX_t)-\lambda^\star|\cdot|A_t-A_t^\star|]

settings.name_in_paper: Model class P^np(s): Hölder nuisance functions on [0,1]^d with sub-Gaussian control errors (upper bound)
unmapped: Asymptotic FDR constraint at level alpha known to learner
Control reference b_0 is conditional mean; control errors uniformly sub-Gaussian; treated outcome CDF Hölder in x uniformly in y
Historical randomized sample of size n_hist
settings.definition_quote: Let $\mathcal P^{\mathrm{np}}(s)$ denote the collection of all distributions satisfying Assumptions 1, 2, and 3 on $\mathcal X=[0,1]^d$ ... take $b_0(\bx)=\Ebb_P\{Y(0)\mid\bX=\bx\}$ and assume that the control errors are uniformly sub-Gaussian

unmapped: Asymptotic FDR constraint at level alpha
Procedures must meet prescribed uniform nuisance-estimation accuracy
Historical randomized sample of size n_hist
settings.definition_quote: define the constrained minimax regret as $\mathfrak R_T(\mathcal P;r_{b,T},r_{F,T}):=\inf_{\mathcal A\in\mathfrak A_T}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\Regret_T(\mathcal A,P)$

symbols.r_T: sum of nuisance estimation rates r_{b,T}+r_{F,T}
symbols.zeta: step-size exponent, eta_t ~ t^-zeta, zeta in (1/2,1)

conditions: Assumptions 1-4 (local density bound near control reference, oracle-score regularity, Hölder model, step sizes)
nuisance estimators satisfy time-averaged uniform MSE rates r_{b,T}, r_{F,T}

source.label: thm:fdr-one-pass
source.quote: Suppose Assumptions~\ref{ass:local-density}--\ref{ass:step-sizes} hold and the nuisance estimators satisfy \eqref{eq:nuisance_rate} ... \max\{|R_T/T-H(\lambda^\star)|,|\FDP_T-\alpha|\}=O_{\Pbb}(r_{T}+T^{-\zeta/2}+\mathfrak H_\chi(T)/T) ... Therefore, when $r_{T}\to0$, we have $\FDR_T\to\alpha$.

results.notes: Bound on FDP deviation from alpha and treatment-rate deviation, in probability (O_P); not a regret bound. Also gives FDR_T -> alpha.

symbols.r_b: time-averaged uniform RMSE rate of control-reference estimator
symbols.r_F: time-averaged uniform RMSE rate of treated-outcome CDF estimator
symbols.eta_bar: average step size sum_t eta_t / T
symbols.eps_bar: average exploration probability sum_t eps_t / T

conditions: nuisance estimators satisfy rate condition (eq. nuisance_rate)

source.label: thm:one-pass-weighted-selection-regret
source.quote: There exists a constant $C<\infty$, independent of $T$, such that ... \Regret_T \le CT\{r_{b,T}^2+r_{F,T}^2+\bar\eta_T+\bar\varepsilon_T+T^{-1}\} for all sufficiently large $T$ ... Consequently, $\Regret_T/T\to0$.

results.notes: Gap-weighted assignment regret relative to FDR-constrained oracle. Theorem also gives an a.s. predictable-regret bound and an O_P version. With spline rates text derives O((log T)^{2s/(2s+d)} T^{(2s+d)/(4s+d)}).

symbols.r_b: prescribed uniform estimation accuracy for control reference
symbols.r_F: prescribed uniform estimation accuracy for treated-outcome CDF
symbols.C_hist: constant depending on C_0 and model-class constants
symbols.n_0hist: expected number of historical control observations
symbols.n_1hist: expected number of historical treated observations

conditions: procedures satisfying asymptotic FDR control limsup FDR_T <= alpha for every P in the class
procedures satisfying uniform time-averaged nuisance MSE bounds <= C_0 r_{b,T}^2 and C_0 r_{F,T}^2
model class P^np(s) on [0,1]^d with Hölder smoothness s and sub-Gaussian control errors

source.label: thm:minimax-nonparametric-fixed
source.quote: For sufficiently small $r_{b,T}$ and $r_{F,T}$, there exist constants $c,C_{\mathrm{hist}}>0$, depending only on $C_0$ and the fixed model-class constants, such that \mathfrak R_T(\mathcal P^{\mathrm{np}}(s);r_{b,T},r_{F,T})\ge c\min\{T,\{r_{b,T}^{-(2s+d)/s}-C_{\mathrm{hist}}n_{0,\mathrm{hist}}\}_++\{r_{F,T}^{-(2s+d)/s}-C_{\mathrm{hist}}n_{1,\mathrm{hist}}\}_+\}

results.notes: Constrained minimax lower bound; s mapped to beta_holder. Paper notes it also holds without the FDR restriction.

conditions: conditions of Theorems 1 and 2 hold with the same constants over P^np(s)
uniform nuisance accuracy sup_P avg E[(delta_b)^2+(delta_F)^2] <= C_nuis rho_T^2

source.label: cor:minimax-nonparametric-rate
source.quote: Suppose $n_{\mathrm{hist}}=O(1)$. Consider $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{PAITS}}$ ... with $\varepsilon_t\asymp t^{-2s/(4s+d)}$ ... PAITS attains the minimax regret rate $T^{(2s+d)/(4s+d)}$ up to logarithmic factors over $\mathcal P^{\mathrm{np}}(s)$, among admissible procedures with prescribed estimation accuracy $r_{b,T}=r_{F,T}=\rho_T$.

results.notes: Explicit upper bound taken from proof of Corollary 2 (eq. minimax-paits-upper), worst case over P^np(s).

conditions: procedures satisfying asymptotic FDR control at level alpha over P^np(s)
procedures satisfying uniform nuisance accuracy r_{b,T}=r_{F,T}=rho_T=(log T)^{s/(2s+d)} T^{-s/(4s+d)}

source.label: cor:minimax-nonparametric-rate
source.quote: For any fixed $C_0\ge C_{\mathrm{nuis}}$, PAITS attains the minimax regret rate $T^{(2s+d)/(4s+d)}$ up to logarithmic factors over $\mathcal P^{\mathrm{np}}(s)$, among admissible procedures with prescribed estimation accuracy $r_{b,T}=r_{F,T}=\rho_T$.

results.notes: Explicit lower-bound expression from the proof (eq. minimax-corollary-lower), a specialization of Theorem 3.
